INTERNATIONAL NATO Secy-General Rutte vows more support for Ukraine By: Agencies Date: September 15, 2026 Share post: WhatsApp Facebook X ReddIt Telegram Linkedin Warsaw, Sep 14: NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said Monday that Russian drone strikes near the Ukraine-Poland border would drive the military alliance to increase its support for Kyiv, calling the attacks on Sunday a sign of growing desperation by the forces under Russian President Vladimir. “The strikes yesterday on trains in Ukraine close to NATO territory again show Putin’s desperation and also his desire to sow fear and terror,” Rutte said at NATO’s political headquarters in Brussels. “Russia is growing increasingly reckless as it continues its terrible war against Ukraine.” Rutte pledged to increase support for Ukraine and bolster the 32-nation alliance’s own defences along its long eastern border with Russia. “He thinks that he can stop us from supporting Ukraine and that he can undermine our unity. He is wrong,” the NATO chief said of Putin. Rutte’s comments came as Poland pledged increased security along its border with Ukraine after a wave of Russian drone strikes near the frontier, including two that landed within kilometres of Polish territory.
